lead: An intent is a message object. It can name one target activity, or name an action for Android to match. It exists so screens and apps can ask for work without hard-coding each other. A restaurant screen can open the dialer, a browser, or a share sheet with the same mechanism. Used in calls, maps, sharing and picking a contact.
prereq: You need Chapter 2.4 for what an activity is and how it is declared.

blocks.text: An intent is an Intent object. It carries a request from one component to another. The system routes an implicit intent; the caller does not choose the process.
Key fields: component names one exact class; action is a verb such as ACTION_VIEW; data is a Uri such as tel:9876543210; extras is a Bundle of key-value pairs; category and type filter matches.

An explicit intent sets component and opens a known screen. An implicit intent sets action, data and often type. Android compares it with intent filters in other apps' manifests. A filter lists accepted actions, categories and data patterns. Only a few universities teach this detail.
If no filter matches, startActivity throws ActivityNotFoundException. The figure shows the call, match and launch.
Use explicit intents for your own screens; use implicit intents for another app's work. The caller never sees the target's class name in an implicit intent.
Use new Intent(this, DetailActivity.class) for your own screen. For another app, set an action.

items: ACTION_DIAL opens the dialer with a number; no permission.
ACTION_VIEW opens a Uri such as https, geo or tel.
ACTION_SEND shares typed content; set the MIME type.
ACTION_SENDTO sends to a Uri such as mailto: or smsto:.
ACTION_PICK asks another app to return a chosen item.

blocks.text: ACTION_DIAL fills the dialer and needs no permission. ACTION_CALL places the call and needs CALL_PHONE.

Common extras keys: EXTRA_TEXT, EXTRA_SUBJECT, EXTRA_EMAIL. Before starting, check intent.resolveActivity(getPackageManager()) != null, or query PackageManager. startActivityForResult is deprecated; use the Activity Result API.
For sharing, createChooser(share, "Send via") shows the app list. Without it Android may use a default, and may throw if no app matches. A chooser is itself an implicit intent wrapper.

figure.caption: The two buttons build two different intents. Call sends ACTION_DIAL with tel:9876543210 straight to the filled dialer; Share sends ACTION_SEND with type text/plain, passes the resolveActivity check, and opens a chooser that sends Table for 4.

spec.title: Two intents from the restaurant screen
spec.aria: A flowchart: the restaurant screen's Call button sends an ACTION_DIAL intent with tel:9876543210 to the dialer, and its Share button sends an ACTION_SEND text/plain intent through a resolveActivity check and a Send via chooser to the picked app, which sends Table for 4.

examples.question: A restaurant screen has two buttons. Call should open the dialer with 9876543210 filled in. Share should send the text Table for 4 to whichever app the user picks. Write both intents and name the checks.
steps: Call intent: action Intent.ACTION_DIAL, data Uri.parse("tel:9876543210"). This fills the dialer. It needs no permission; the user presses call.
Do not use ACTION_CALL: it places the call directly and needs CALL_PHONE.
Wrap it: startActivity(Intent.createChooser(share, "Send via")). The chooser lists apps and avoids a silent default.
Check share.resolveActivity(getPackageManager()) != null before starting; otherwise ActivityNotFoundException can occur.
examples.answer: Call uses ACTION_DIAL with tel:9876543210; Share uses ACTION_SEND, type text/plain, extra Table for 4, inside createChooser.

traps: Starting an implicit intent without a resolveActivity or PackageManager check causes ActivityNotFoundException.
Using ACTION_CALL where ACTION_DIAL is enough: direct call and missing CALL_PHONE permission.
Forgetting setType on ACTION_SEND: many share apps will not match.
Putting a Uri in extras when it belongs in data: intent-filter matching fails.
Sending an explicit intent to another app's private activity: SecurityException.

quiz.a: A message object that names a component or an action.

quiz.q: Why does Android use intent filters?
quiz.a: They let apps advertise accepted implicit intents without the caller naming a class.

quiz.q: Write an explicit intent from MainActivity to DetailActivity.
Write an implicit intent to open a geo Uri for Chennai 13.0827, 80.2707.

quiz.a: The MIME type is missing, so matching apps may not appear and the chooser can be empty.
It shows the app list, avoids a hidden default, and handles many targets.

quiz.q: Which action opens the dialer with a number?

beyond: Not for the exam. Intents also carry deep links, PendingIntent alarms and share sheets. Modern Android adds App Links verification and stricter exported-component rules. Security reviews look for intent redirection and leaked PendingIntent. Search next for Android implicit intent security and Activity Result contracts.
